rv.q: Skinner's play, which starts so promisingly, ends by making Linda seem a victim of hapless circumstance rather than a tragic archetype.

This does not prevent the play landing with unabated comic force most of the time, despite the inevitable hiccups of a half-achieved (at the moment) central performance; miraculously, Dumezweni makes most of her scenes work through pluck and naked technique.
Despite some good satirical points, and some good jokes, Skinner takes the temperature of the times with a rather insensitive thermometer, one which is frustratingly unsubtle.

cn.t: Penelope Skinner's play about ageism and female invisibility starts strong but ultimately undermines its own message, though Noma Dumezweni earns praise for heroically stepping into the lead role at short notice.
